message.content:
`docker start` is **not** the command that brings up the Docker daemon – it only starts an existing container. To bring the Docker service (the daemon) up on Windows you have two common options: | What you want | How to do it | |---------------|--------------| | **Start the Docker Desktop GUI** (recommended if you installed Docker Desktop) | ```powershell
& "C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"
``` | | **Start the Docker Engine service directly** (works for Docker Desktop or Docker Engine installed as a Windows Service) | ```powershell
Start-Service Docker # or
net start com.docker.service
``` | ### Quick steps 1. **Open PowerShell as Administrator** *Right‑click → Run as administrator.* 2. **Start the service** ```powershell Start-Service Docker ``` *If you prefer the legacy command:* ```powershell net start com.docker.service ``` 3. **Verify** ```powershell docker version ``` You should see client and server versions printed – the server part confirms Docker is running. ### If you just want to start a container Once the daemon is running, you can start a container with: ```powershell docker start ``` Replace `` with the actual name or ID of the container you wish to start. --- **TL;DR:** - Use `Start-Service Docker` (or `net start com.docker.service`) to start the Docker daemon. - Use `docker start ` to start a specific container.
